newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end mostly up in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end mostly up in quiet trade.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures ended mostly firmer on Friday, reflecting a moderate recovery in bullion prices during Asian hours, traders said.
Trade was thin as private investors retreated to the sidelines due to Easter holidays in overseas markets.

Most of gold futures ended up except for the May contract, which was thinly traded. Benchmark February gold was up six yen at 1,385. "Amid uncertainty over the direction in the currency market and spot gold prices after the holidays, activity was mainly dominated by position-adjustments by trade houses," one trader said.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $350.00/40 per ounce at the Tokyo close, after opening at 349.60/350.00 and Thursday's New York level of $348.00/50.
Platinum futures ended mixed, while palladium futures were mostly firmer on private investors' short-covering ahead of the close.

In platinum futures, trade house selling before the weekend dented distant months, the traders said. "Market players were still waiting for new information from Russia as to when the Japan-Russia export talks of platinum group metals will be held," one analyst at a commodity broker said.

Palladium imports in February amounted to 9.308 tonnes, Finance Ministry data showed. The figures were lower than the unusually high level of 10.39 tonnes last February, but higher than the usual monthly level of six tonnes.

"The high imports showed that Japanese traders boosted spot purchases due to expectations of the delay in Japan-Russia talks," one bullion house source said. Benchmark February palladium was up five yen at 569 yen. Benchmark February platinum was down one yen at 1,460 yen.
Benchmark February silver was down 0.3 yen per 10 grams at 204.0 yen.
